subject: engine oil
title: What If You Never Changed Your Car's Oil?

scenes.text: What if you never changed your car's oil? The engine wouldn't die fast. It would die from inside.
AAA says most cars need fresh oil every 5,000 to 7,500 miles. After that, its protective additives wear out.
Over thousands of miles, dirt and soot clog the filter. A bypass valve sends dirty oil around it.
Then the oil thickens into black sludge, like tar, and starts blocking the narrow passages that feed the engine.
With no slippery film left, metal rubs on metal. Friction turns into heat, and wear speeds up.
Eventually hot parts can weld together and the engine seizes for good. Even a parked car needs fresh oil once a year.

description:
What if you never changed your car's oil? Additives wear out, dirt bypasses a clogged filter, oil turns to sludge, and metal-on-metal friction can finally seize the engine.
AAA suggests changing oil every 5,000 to 7,500 miles, and at least once a year.
